# Heat and temperature regulation — function ontology

**Card 12 · source workbook `ontology/xlsx/Nature_Heat_Temperature_Regulation_Ontology_Integrated_v1.xlsx` · generated by `scripts/build-knowledge.js` — do not edit by hand.**

## Scope boundary

The whole thermal domain in one card, in two layers. The control layer (NT strategies) covers insulation, countercurrent exchange, storage, set-point management and adaptive regulation — how a system holds a temperature. The heat-removal layer (NC strategies) covers evaporative, radiative, conductive and convective cooling — how a system sheds heat, and it is a child of the control layer, not a sibling. When the question is 'stay within a band', start at NT. When it is 'get rid of heat', start at NC and check which NT strategy it serves. The standalone cooling workbook was retired; this file supersedes it.

## Challenge triggers — control layer

| Challenge | Prioritise | Reasoning rule |
|---|---|---|
| External solar load dominates | NT01 | Prevent heat entry before designing rejection. |
| Need passive outdoor sub-ambient cooling | NT01; NT02 | Combine solar rejection with thermal emission and weather-aware screening. |
| Need same surface to warm in winter and cool in su… | NT03 | Use switchable absorptance/emissivity rather than compromise fixed coating. |
| Large exposed radiator available but heat loss mus… | NT04 | Control thermal conductance with flow rather than changing radiator size. |
| Need heat conservation in circulating-fluid system | NT05 | Use counter-current recovery before external exchange. |
| High heat flux and dry/ventilated ambient | NT06 | Exploit latent heat, but explicitly account for water and vapor sink. |
| Limited liquid supply; surface dries too fast | NT07 | Increase residence time and wetted area before increasing liquid flow. |
| Intermittent heat spikes with idle periods | NT08 | Separate high-power discharge from low-load recharge. |
| Need autonomous vent/transpiration control without… | NT09 | Put feedback into local aperture state. |
| Distributed hotspots and limited pumping | NT10 | Design branch topology and proximity from heat map, not uniform spacing. |
| Building/enclosure has strong day/night swing or w… | NT11 | Use thermal phase lag and pressure gradients as passive pumping. |
| Cold system can reconfigure geometry | NT12 | Reduce exposed area/increase density before adding heating energy. |
| Need lightweight passive insulation | NT13 | Trap many small gas pockets and protect them mechanically. |
| Peak heat can be tolerated temporarily | NT14 | Use allowable temperature swing as storage before adding peak cooling. |
| Critical component needs tighter temperature than… | NT15 | Sense and allocate thermal effort to vulnerable region first. |
| Environment changes faster than passive equilibrium | NT15 | Use thresholded multi-mode control; rank lowest-cost response first. |
| Need both cooling and heat conservation over season | NT03; NT13 | Combine adaptive surface with controllable conductance/insulation. |
| Water use must be near zero | NT01; NT02; NT11; NT13; NT14 | THM01; THM13; THM18 |
| High humidity limits evaporation | NT02; NT10; NT11 | Shift to radiation/flow/prevention rather than scaling water flow. |
| System experiences large thermal transients but av… | NT14; NT08 | Pair thermal mass with rechargeable latent/sorption storage. |

## Maturity guide

| Level | Label | Definition | Does NOT prove |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Concept / biological mech… | Natural mechanism characterized or engineering concept proposed | Engineering feasibility or manufacturability |
| 2 | Modeled / simulated | Engineering geometry/material evaluated computationally | Fabricated performance or durability |
| 3 | Lab demonstration | Prototype/material tested under controlled conditions | Field reliability, scale, economics |
| 4 | Pilot / relevant field | Prototype tested in realistic environment/process | Scaled commercial supply chain |
| 5 | Product / in market | Solution deployed commercially with documented operation | Universal performance in all contexts |
